newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 29.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Fraud Office called in to probe ACC after audit: The Serious Fraud Office is to investigate alleged "irregularities" involving ACC -- matters the corporation's minister, Jenny Shipley, described as being of "deep concern". Page 1.
Ministry seeks possible CJD victims: The Health Ministry is starting a newspaper campaign to trace New Zealanders who may be at risk of contracting Creutzfeldt Jakob disease. Page 1.

Indecision on trout cowardly -- Labour: The government was too cowardly to take a potentially coalition-splitting decision on whether to join an appeal against a court ruling that Maoris could fish trout without a licence in some circumstances, Labour's Maori affairs spokesman Dover Samuels and senior MP Mike Moore said on Wednesday. Page 2.

Student loan write-offs predicted to reach $106m: Student loan write-offs were expected to reach $106 million by 2000 with $18 million written off already, Alliance education spokeswoman Liz Gordon said on Wednesday. Page 2.

Health authorities reneging on abortion, MPs told: Some health authorities were trying to get out of their obligations to provide abortion services for women, Abortion Supervisory Committee chairwoman Christine Forster said on Wednesday. Page 2.

TransAlta does much better: Wellington power company TransAlta NZ reported on Wednesday a better-than-expected $7.2 million profit for the half-year to March 31, and expects to achieve full merger benefits a year ahead of schedule. Page 13.

Manufacturing decline decried: After 28,000 jobs were lost last year, the manufacturing industry is headed "downhill all the way" if present policies continue, according to a report commissioned by the Engineers Union. Page 14.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD
Huge bill for defects in Navy vessel: Defence chiefs are faced with a $30 million bill to turn their only cargo ship into an effective military vessel.

Ceramco springs surprise payout: Diversified apparel, mining and investment company Ceramco Corporation on Wednesday surprised equally analysts by reporting a $964,000 March-year profit and recommending a final dividend of 7.5 cents a share.

ANZ sees interest earnings erode: ANZ Bank's New Zealand operations have produced a little-changed interim profit after a credit on bad debts and stronger non-lending income only just countered the impact of lower lending margins.
Hollywood contacts kiwi firm: A Wellington visual effects company has struck a deal to supply computer generated effects for a new Hollywood film.

Clear switches on business phones: Clear Communications on Wednesday launched its local business service, saying it heralded a new era of choice at least for firms in the central business districts of Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch.
THE PRESS
Club vows to do better after audit: Papanui Working Men's Club members vowed on Wednesday night to make the club stronger and more efficient after a damaging report on its financial affairs. Page 1.
Rickard scorns Maori male MPs: Veteran Maori rights campaigner Eva Rickard has hit out at New Zealand First's male Maori MPs. Page 1.

Support for Labour up: National's woes continued on Wednesday night with the latest poll showing that combined support for it and coalition partner New Zealand First was nine points less than Labour. Page 3.
NZ bonds hold edge: New Zealand's reputation as a quality destination for bond investors is expected to survive rising long-term interest rates this year. Page 29.
Sale of Chch sections going well, says CDL: The development projects of CDL Investments in Christchurch are prominent in its the strategy. Page 29.
Another tough year for Fruitfed: A difficult year for horticulture is reflected in Fruitfed Supplies' annual profit, down by a quarter on last year. Page 29.
